researched_by: the council's own camping, clearway, traffic-order and campervan waste pages, the text of its off-street car parks order, a 2013 committee report establishing ownership of Aberfeldy Caravan Park, Courier reporting on the clearways and the Pitlochry signage, and campsite directories for the caravan park's coordinates and season
policy_summary:
The gateway to the Highlands, and one of the most restrictive regimes in Scotland once you look past the tourism copy. Perth and Kinross has no aire, no overnight bays and no campervan scheme of any kind. What it has is a car parks order that bans sleeping outright and a growing network of rural clearways on the roads people actually want to stop on.

The order is the thing to know. Article 29 of the Perth and Kinross Council (Off-Street Car Parks) Order says 'No person shall use any part of a car park or any vehicle left in a car park for sleeping, camping, or light or cause or permit to be lit any fire for cooking purposes.' That is a blanket sleeping prohibition across every council car park in the area, not a sign on one seafront. Article 4(c) adds a 72-hour maximum stay. The order's definition of 'caravan' - 'a vehicle designed or adapted for human habitation' - catches motorhomes as well as touring caravans, which matters at the three Perth car parks where caravans are banned at all times. Enforcement is decriminalised: GBP100, halved to GBP50 inside 14 days.

The clearways are the second half. Temporary orders went up across Highland Perthshire in summer 2021 after weekends when more than a hundred vehicles lined the roads around Lochs Tay, Tummel and Rannoch, and were made permanent by the Perth and Kinross Council (Rural Clearways) Order 2022. Twelve roads and verges are now no-stopping: C450 Kinloch Rannoch to Tomphubil, A827 Aberfeldy Road at Kenmore, C451, Pier Road Kenmore, C448 Fortingall to Bridge of Balgie through Glen Lyon, B487 Calvine to Trinafour, A923 Blairgowrie to Dunkeld, C430 and C432 at Loch Clunie, C452 Foss to Pitlochry, U111 Mains of Clunie to Concraigie, and Linn Road at Stanley. A further clearway order covering Dunkeld, Killichonan and Kenmore was advertised 8 to 29 May 2026, so the network is still growing.

The one thing the council has built is a waste point. Black and grey water disposal opened at Broxden Park and Ride on the Glasgow Road approach to Perth - the first facility of its kind in Perth and Kinross - open 24 hours from Easter weekend to the end of October, currently free with a charge signalled. It is a service point, not a stopover: Article 29 applies to Broxden like every other council car park.

And there is a campsite the parking pages never mention. Aberfeldy Caravan Park on the banks of the Tay is council-owned - a 2013 committee report settles the title, having gone looking for it in the Aberfeldy Common Good Fund and found instead that the land was bought by the former burgh for a sewage works. It is a full touring park with a motorhome service point, open mid-March to late October, and nothing on the council's parking or camping pages links to it.
notes:
THE SHAPE OF THIS ONE IS RESTRICTION WITHOUT PROVISION, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF SOUTH AYRSHIRE. Ayr answered a pollution problem by building bays and then signing the streets. Perth and Kinross has signed the streets, banned sleeping in every car park it owns, and built one waste tap forty miles south of the pressure. The pressure is at Kenmore, Killiecrankie, Glen Lyon and Rannoch; the tap is at a park and ride on the Perth ring road. The council's own FAQ is candid about why it has not gone further the other way either: it rejected byelaws because they have a 'lengthy implementation process' and there is 'limited evidence that these measures are effective'. So no byelaws, but a hard parking order and a widening clearway net.

PITLOCHRY IS WHERE THE POLICY BECAME VISIBLE. The council put red signs up in the Ferry Road car park reading 'Strictly no overnight sleeping, camping or cooking in the car park', and the town was promptly branded the country's most unwelcoming. The stated reason was fire: Scottish Fire and Rescue recommends a six-metre gap between motorhomes, and vans were parking less than a metre apart, with a 2019 Oban motorhome fire cited as the precedent. That is the same argument Lincoln used in England. It is worth recording that the signs are not new law - Article 29 already said it - they are the council deciding to enforce a rule it has had all along.

THE SCOTTISH POINT, AGAIN. The council's informal camping FAQ states plainly that 'outdoor access rights do not extend to any motorised activities'. The Land Reform (Scotland) Act 2003 and the Scottish Outdoor Access Code give a walker a right to pitch a tent for two or three nights. They give a van nothing. Perth and Kinross is the third Scottish file in a row to say so in its own words, after Loch Lomond and the Cairngorms.

ON THE CAIRNGORMS CLAIM, WHICH I WAS ASKED TO CHECK. Both halves of what data/sites/cairngorms-national-park.json records hold up. Glenshee Ski Centre is privately run - its own booking pages confirm GBP8 a night without hook-up, GBP15 a day with, GBP5 each for chemical and grey waste, no tents and no caravans, at Cairnwell, Braemar AB35 5XU. And there is no local-authority provision inside the park from this council: nothing in the Perth and Kinross share of the Cairngorms - Blair Atholl, Glen Tilt, Calvine, the Spittal of Glenshee, the Cairnwell - is a council overnight facility, and the same Article 29 sleeping ban that covers Perth covers any council car park up there too. The Cairngorms record's own price note is right; the only wrinkle is that its top-level arrival_from of 17:00 applies to hook-up bookings only, since the operator lets non-hook-up pitches arrive any time and leave by 10am. Not worth a correction, but worth knowing.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY AVAILABLE HERE BELONGS TO SOMEBODY ELSE. Forestry and Land Scotland's Stay the Night scheme has six car parks in Tay Forest Park - Allt Druidhe and Talladh-a-Bheithe on Loch Rannoch, Lower Bohespic at Tummel Bridge, Drummond Hill, Douglas Fir Wood and Tonguey Faulds. Those are FLS's, not the council's, and they sit in exactly the country the clearways closed off. Anyone mapping Highland Perthshire needs the FLS record alongside this one or the picture is wrong.

Last, a note on private supply so nobody re-researches it. Blair Castle Caravan Park is Atholl Estates, Milton of Fonab at Pitlochry and Blairgowrie Holiday Park are commercial, and Scone Palace is the Camping and Caravanning Club on estate land. Aberfeldy is the only one this council owns.
open_questions: Coordinates. Only Aberfeldy Caravan Park could be corroborated this session - Broxden Park and Ride and the Ferry Road car park at Pitlochry are recorded with null geometry and need a pin from park4night, campercontact or the council's own map before they can be published.

Is Aberfeldy Caravan Park still under direct council management in 2026? The 2013 report says the council would keep managing it if a lease could not be arranged, and no lease has been found - but 2025 reviews complain of no on-site staff, which reads like a remotely run operation. The operator's own site names nobody.

Current Aberfeldy pitch counts and prices. The operator says 133 hardstanding plus 31 grass, ukcampsite says 102, ACSI says 176 touring plus 73 permanent. Nobody agrees and the council publishes nothing.
When does the Broxden waste charge arrive, and how much? The council says a charge 'will be implemented in the future' but has not said when.
The Dunkeld, Killichonan and Kenmore clearway order advertised 8-29 May 2026 - was it made, and what does it cover? This record has a known expiry.

Is there any consolidated in-force text of the Off-Street Car Parks Order online? Article 29 was read from the Variation No 9 order, which restates the principal order's articles; the principal order itself was not located.
Whether the Kinloch Rannoch community aire proposal that CAMpRA recorded as withdrawn has been revived. Nothing found for 2026.
Whether any of the twelve clearway roads carries an exemption for stopping to load, and whether the council enforces them outside the summer.

sites.name: Aberfeldy Caravan Park
sites.price_note: Around GBP30 a night for a motorhome pitch in 2026 on booking-site listings; electricity is metered separately at about GBP0.53 per kWh. The council publishes no tariff of its own.
sites.search_hint: Aberfeldy Caravan Park, Dunkeld Road, Aberfeldy PH15 2AQ
sites.notes: THE PROVISION THE PARKING PAGES DO NOT MENTION. A council-owned touring park on the north bank of the Tay, two minutes' walk from Aberfeldy square, and the only overnight facility Perth and Kinross Council owns anywhere. Nothing on the council's parking, camping or tourism pages links to it and the site trades under its own name and its own booking line, so from the council's website it is invisible. Ownership is settled by a January 2013 committee report which went looking for the land in the Aberfeldy Common Good Fund and concluded it was not a common good asset because the former burgh had bought it for a sewage treatment plant; the same report records a 2012 decision to market a lease and to keep the site in council management if none could be agreed. Takes tents, caravans, motorhomes and campervans. Pitch counts and prices vary wildly between directories - see open questions.

sites.price_note: Free at present; the council says a charge will be implemented in future.
sites.search_hint: Broxden Park and Ride campervan waste disposal, Glasgow Road, Perth
sites.notes: A SERVICE POINT, NOT A STOPOVER - and the distinction matters here more than anywhere, because Article 29 of the car parks order bans sleeping at Broxden exactly as it does everywhere else the council owns. The first facility of its kind in Perth and Kinross, built in response to post-pandemic campervan numbers. On the south side of the park and ride behind the waiting room, signposted from the main road, by the Broxden roundabout on the Glasgow Road approach to Perth; users place it in the bottom corner of the upper car park below the EV charging hub. Open 24 hours a day from Easter weekend to the end of October. There is no attendant - you phone the council for the access code. Geometry not corroborated this session, so it carries no pin yet.

sites.name: Lay-bys and roads in Perth and Kinross outside the clearways
sites.notes: Where the council has not made a clearway, on-road overnight parking is not prohibited by this authority, and the council marks some lay-bys with blue P signs for 'responsible parking' - though its own clearway page admits they 'fill up quickly'. Its informal camping FAQ frames the limits in road traffic terms rather than access terms: do not block entrances or make roads difficult to use, do not park in passing places or on clearways, do not damage verges, and obey car park terms and conditions which 'may prohibit overnight stays'. It is explicit that outdoor access rights 'do not extend to any motorised activities' - the Land Reform (Scotland) Act 2003 gives a tent a right it does not give a van. So this is the absence of a prohibition, not a permission.

sites.name: All Perth and Kinross Council car parks - no sleeping, camping or cooking fires
sites.notes: THE HEADLINE RESTRICTION, AND IT IS IN THE ORDER RATHER THAN ON A SIGN. Article 29: 'No person shall use any part of a car park or any vehicle left in a car park for sleeping, camping, or light or cause or permit to be lit any fire for cooking purposes.' It bites on every off-street car park the council operates, everywhere in Perth and Kinross including its share of the Cairngorms National Park, and it restricts SLEEPING rather than parking - the vehicle may stand there, you may not sleep in it. Article 4(c) separately caps any stay at 72 consecutive hours. Decriminalised enforcement: GBP100, reduced to GBP50 if paid within 14 days. Text read from the Variation No 9 order advertised in 2025, which restates the principal order's articles.

sites.name: Ferry Road Car Park, Pitlochry
sites.notes: The place where the paper rule became a red sign. The council installed signs reading 'Strictly no overnight sleeping, camping or cooking in the car park' after campervans massed here - an earlier count put more than forty in one Pitlochry car park - and Pitlochry was promptly labelled the country's most unwelcoming town. The stated reason is fire spread, not nuisance: Scottish Fire and Rescue advises a six-metre gap between motorhomes, as on a campsite, and vans were parking under a metre apart. No new instrument was needed; Article 29 of the car parks order already prohibited it. Recorded separately from the estate-wide record because it is the one named car park where the council has chosen to advertise the rule. Coordinates not corroborated this session - no pin yet.

sites.name: Perth city centre car parks where caravans and motorhomes are banned outright
sites.notes: At Library East, Library West, Drumhar Court and South Inch in Perth the order prohibits heavy goods vehicles, caravans and small trailers AT ALL TIMES - a parking ban, not just a sleeping ban. The catch for van users is the order's definition: a 'caravan' is 'a vehicle designed or adapted for human habitation', which takes in motorhomes and converted campervans as readily as towed caravans. South Inch matters most in practice because it is the large riverside car park people are steered towards for Perth. Read from the Variation No 9 order schedule; the individual car park entries should be checked against on-site signage.

sites.name: Rural clearways on twelve Highland Perthshire roads
sites.search_hint: Perth and Kinross Council rural clearways Kenmore Glen Lyon Loch Rannoch
sites.notes: NO STOPPING, not merely no parking - the council's page says you are 'not allowed to stop or park, even briefly', on the carriageway or the verge. The twelve lengths are: C450 Kinloch Rannoch to Tomphubil; A827 Aberfeldy Road, Kenmore; C451 from the A827 Kenmore to Aberfeldy junction; Pier Road, Kenmore; C448 Fortingall to Bridge of Balgie, which is the Glen Lyon road; B487 Calvine to Trinafour; A923 Blairgowrie to Dunkeld; C430 Loch Clunie to Mains of Clunie; C452 Foss to Pitlochry; Linn Road, Stanley; U111 Mains of Clunie to Concraigie; and C432 Loch Clunie to Wester Essendy Road. Introduced as temporary orders in summer 2021 after weekends when more than a hundred vehicles lined the roads around Lochs Tay, Tummel and Rannoch, and made permanent by the Rural Clearways Order 2022. Ramblers Scotland called them disproportionate and Mountaineering Scotland a 'blunt prohibition'; the council defended them as keeping narrow rural roads clear for emergency and farm vehicles. Enforced by the council's parking attendants and by Police Scotland. A further clearway order covering Dunkeld, Killichonan and Kenmore was advertised 8-29 May 2026, so the list is not final. Linear restrictions, so no pin.
